name: Software Development
summary: Coding agents are among AI's largest commercial uses, with multi-billion run rates and a major acquisition. Agents are spreading into review, security, incident response and legacy migration, while productivity evidence stays mixed.

regions.name: Coding agents
regions.summary: Terminal, IDE and cloud agents that write, run and fix code across whole repos. Claude Code, Codex and Cursor lead a fast-growing market that is now consolidating.
regions.whyItMatters: This is where AI earns the most revenue today and where claims about automating knowledge work are tested first.
regions.openQuestion: How much real productivity do coding agents add once review, rework and selection effects are counted?

landmarks.name: Claude Code run rate passes $2.5B
landmarks.summary: Anthropic's Series G announcement said Claude Code run-rate revenue was over $2.5B, more than double the start of 2026, with enterprise use over half.

landmarks.name: SpaceX completes Cursor acquisition
landmarks.summary: Cursor said SpaceX had completed its acquisition, a process that began in April 2026 with a model-training partnership. The price was reported as $60B in stock.
landmarks.note: Price is from press reports cited on Wikipedia, not from Cursor's post.

landmarks.name: GPT-5.3-Codex launched
landmarks.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5.3-Codex, which it describes as a Codex-native agent pairing frontier coding performance with general reasoning for long-horizon technical work.
landmarks.note: Confirmed in OpenAI's news feed; the article page itself blocks scripts.

landmarks.name: METR revisits developer slowdown study
landmarks.summary: METR said developers are likely more sped up by AI than in its 2025 study, but selection effects make the new data weak evidence, so it is changing the study design.

deepDives.title: SWE-bench Leaderboards
deepDives.why: Scores for resolving real GitHub issues, including a like-for-like Bash Only view.

deepDives.title: Terminal-Bench
deepDives.why: Leaderboard of agents on hard terminal tasks, with cost and tokens per run.

deepDives.title: METR: Early-2025 AI and experienced open-source developers
deepDives.why: The randomised trial in which 16 developers took 19% longer with early-2025 tools.

deepDives.title: Simon Willison on coding agents
deepDives.why: A practitioner's running notes on what coding agents can and cannot do.

regions.name: Code review
regions.summary: AI reviewers comment on pull requests to keep pace with the volume of AI-written code. Pure-play vendors raise large rounds while model labs ship their own reviewers.
regions.whyItMatters: As agents write more code, human review becomes the bottleneck, so automated review decides how fast teams can safely ship.
regions.openQuestion: Can AI reviewers be trusted to check AI-written code, or do they share the same blind spots?

landmarks.name: Anthropic Code Review for Claude Code
landmarks.summary: Multi-agent PR reviewer in research preview for Team and Enterprise. Anthropic said PRs with substantive review comments rose from 16% to 54% internally.

landmarks.name: CodeRabbit raises $143M at $1.5B
landmarks.summary: Series C co-led by Atomico and Smash Capital, announced with a new 'Agentic Change Management' product that goes beyond AI code review.

landmarks.name: Cursor reports Bugbot gains
landmarks.summary: Cursor said 40 experiments since Bugbot's July 2025 launch raised the share of flagged bugs that get resolved from 52% to over 70%. Self-reported.

landmarks.name: Greptile $25M Series A
landmarks.summary: Benchmark-led round for a code review agent startup, announced with a v3 rewrite that the company says catches 3x more critical bugs than v2.

deepDives.title: Automating Code Review Activities by Large-Scale Pre-training
deepDives.why: The CodeReviewer paper that framed review as tasks a model can learn and be scored on.

deepDives.title: Google Research: Resolving code review comments with ML
deepDives.why: How a large engineering organisation deployed ML-suggested edits in review.

deepDives.title: Greptile: AI Code Review Benchmarks 2025
deepDives.why: Five review tools on 50 real bugs. Run by a vendor, so read it with care.

deepDives.title: Claude Code Action
deepDives.why: Open-source action showing how agent PR review is wired into a repository.

regions.name: Testing & QA
regions.summary: Incumbent test vendors and startups ship agents that explore apps, write and maintain tests, and file bugs. Performance claims are mostly vendor-reported.
regions.whyItMatters: More AI-written code needs more verification, and testing is the cheapest place to catch what agents get wrong.
regions.openQuestion: Will teams trust autonomous test agents enough to drop scripted suites, given the lack of independent results?

landmarks.name: SmartBear BearQ
landmarks.summary: Agentic QA system from a testing incumbent that explores web applications and builds and maintains tests on its own, later added to Jira as an assignable agent.

landmarks.name: Tricentis agentic QE platform
landmarks.summary: Tricentis launched an agentic quality engineering platform with an AI Workspace that orchestrates and governs testing agents, plus pre-built agents.

landmarks.name: Momentic Mo scriptless QA agent
landmarks.summary: Agent that tests web, iOS and Android apps from a brief instead of scripts, then reports what failed with steps to reproduce and video evidence.

deepDives.title: SWT-Bench leaderboard
deepDives.why: Scores agents on writing tests that reproduce real GitHub issues.

deepDives.title: Automated Unit Test Improvement using LLMs at Meta
deepDives.why: Industrial study of LLM-written tests with filters that guarantee measurable improvement.

deepDives.title: Playwright MCP
deepDives.why: The widely used open-source bridge that lets agents drive a browser for testing.

deepDives.title: Momentic docs: Mo
deepDives.why: Concrete view of how an exploratory QA agent is set up and when to use it.

regions.name: Observability & SRE
regions.summary: AI SRE agents investigate alerts, test root-cause hypotheses against telemetry and suggest fixes. Vendors ship them as GA products, while open benchmarks show modest scores.
regions.whyItMatters: Incident response is a high-stakes test of whether agents can reason over live systems, not only over code.
regions.openQuestion: When can an agent be allowed to remediate production incidents itself rather than only investigate?

landmarks.name: Datadog Bits AI SRE generally available
landmarks.summary: Autonomous agent that investigates alerts across logs, traces and metrics. Datadog says it was tested against more than 2,000 customer environments.

landmarks.name: AWS DevOps Agent generally available
landmarks.summary: AWS agent that investigates and helps prevent incidents across AWS, multicloud and on-prem, with Azure support added at GA after a December 2025 preview.

landmarks.name: ITBench: agents resolve 13.8% of SRE tasks
landmarks.summary: IBM-led benchmark of 94 real-world IT scenarios found agents resolved 13.8% of SRE, 25.2% of compliance and security, and 0% of FinOps scenarios.

deepDives.title: ITBench-AA Benchmark (Artificial Analysis)
deepDives.why: Independent leaderboard on 59 Kubernetes incident tasks; top models score just over half.

deepDives.title: AIOpsLab: evaluating AI agents for autonomous clouds
deepDives.why: Microsoft framework for testing agents on injected cloud faults.

deepDives.title: Datadog: Introducing Bits Investigation
deepDives.why: How a production SRE agent forms and tests root-cause hypotheses.

deepDives.title: ITBench
deepDives.why: Open scenarios and code for SRE, compliance and FinOps agent evaluation.

regions.name: AppSec & vulnerability finding
regions.summary: Models now find real vulnerabilities at scale. Labs ship code-scanning agents in preview, and an autonomous pentester topped a bug bounty leaderboard.
regions.whyItMatters: The same capability that finds and patches flaws for defenders also lowers the cost of finding them for attackers.
regions.openQuestion: Will AI vulnerability discovery favor defenders, or will fixes lag behind the volume of flaws found?

landmarks.name: Claude Code Security
landmarks.summary: Anthropic codebase scanner that suggests patches for human review, in limited research preview. Anthropic said Opus 4.6 found over 500 flaws in open-source code.

landmarks.name: Codex Security research preview
landmarks.summary: OpenAI opened a research preview of Codex Security, an agent that detects, validates and patches vulnerabilities. It follows the Aardvark private beta of October 2025.
landmarks.note: Confirmed in OpenAI's news feed; the article page itself blocks scripts.

landmarks.name: Google Big Sleep reports 20 bugs
landmarks.summary: Google's DeepMind and Project Zero agent reported its first 20 vulnerabilities in open-source software, found by the agent and checked by a human before reporting.

landmarks.name: XBOW tops HackerOne US leaderboard
landmarks.summary: XBOW said its autonomous pentesting agent reached the top of HackerOne's US leaderboard, a first for an AI system, with findings confirmed by program owners.

deepDives.title: CyberGym: AI agents' real-world cybersecurity capabilities
deepDives.why: Large-scale evaluation of agents on real vulnerability analysis tasks.

deepDives.title: Frontier AI Cybersecurity Observatory
deepDives.why: Open tracker of AI capability across stages of attack and defence.

deepDives.title: Project Zero: From Naptime to Big Sleep
deepDives.why: First-hand account of an agent finding an exploitable SQLite bug.

deepDives.title: XBOW: The Road to Top 1
deepDives.why: Running an autonomous pentester against live bounty programs, and how findings are validated.

regions.name: CI/CD & platform engineering
regions.summary: Coding agents are being wired into CI to triage issues, fix failing builds and update docs. Platforms add sandboxing and permissions but the tooling is still in preview.
regions.whyItMatters: CI is where agents get standing access to repositories, so its guardrails set how much autonomy teams can safely grant.
regions.openQuestion: Can permission and sandbox models make unattended agents safe enough for build and release pipelines?

landmarks.name: GitHub Agentic Workflows technical preview
landmarks.summary: Markdown-defined workflows run coding agents (Copilot, Claude Code, Codex) in GitHub Actions, read-only by default with pre-approved 'safe outputs' for writes.

landmarks.name: Register: use at your own risk
landmarks.summary: The Register's coverage noted GitHub's own 'use at your own risk' advice alongside its claim that guardrails beat running agent CLIs directly in Actions.

landmarks.name: Agentic Workflows reach public preview
landmarks.summary: GitHub moved Agentic Workflows from technical preview to public preview about four months after first release.

landmarks.name: AWS frontier agents announced
landmarks.summary: At re:Invent AWS previewed three long-running 'frontier agents': the Kiro autonomous agent, AWS Security Agent and AWS DevOps Agent.

deepDives.title: GitHub blog: Automate repository tasks with Agentic Workflows
deepDives.why: GitHub's own walkthrough of running coding agents inside CI with guardrails.

deepDives.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows documentation
deepDives.why: Reference for the open-source tool: workflow format, safe outputs, sandbox and firewall.

deepDives.title: GitHub Next: Continuous AI
deepDives.why: The research framing behind automated AI in repositories, by analogy with CI/CD.

deepDives.title: DORA: State of AI-assisted Software Development 2025
deepDives.why: Survey-based research on how AI adoption relates to delivery performance.

regions.name: Legacy migration & modernization
regions.summary: Agents read COBOL and mainframe code, extract business rules and draft rewrites. IBM and the major clouds now sell agentic modernization, and markets have reacted.
regions.whyItMatters: Decades-old code runs banking, insurance and government, and cheaper migration would shift large services revenues.
regions.openQuestion: Can AI-led rewrites be proven equivalent to the original systems well enough for regulated industries?

landmarks.name: IBM stock drops on Anthropic COBOL post
landmarks.summary: IBM shares fell 13.2% in a day, the most since October 2000, after Anthropic said Claude Code could be used to modernize COBOL running on IBM systems.
landmarks.note: Reuters report, read in a syndicated copy.

landmarks.name: IBM Bob multi-agent modernization
landmarks.summary: IBM added multi-agent capabilities, AI cost and use analytics, and Premium Packages of workflows for IBM Z, IBM i and Java modernization to its Bob platform.

landmarks.name: Google mainframe modernization agents
landmarks.summary: Google paired business-rule extraction in its Mainframe Assessment Tool with Mainframe Modernization Agents that forward-engineer rewritten applications.

deepDives.title: Martin Fowler: Legacy Modernization meets GenAI
deepDives.why: Practitioner account of using LLMs to understand legacy code before rewriting it.

deepDives.title: Google Cloud: Mainframe Modernization solutions
deepDives.why: Shows the assess, rewrite and validate pipeline a hyperscaler now sells.

deepDives.title: Legacy Modernization Agents: COBOL to Java/C#
deepDives.why: Open-source agent migration pipeline from Microsoft that you can read and run.

deepDives.title: AWS CardDemo mainframe application
deepDives.why: A public COBOL application commonly used to demonstrate and compare migration tools.

regions.name: Specs, design-to-code & prototyping
regions.summary: Prompt-to-app builders grow fast among non-engineers, design tools generate working code, and spec-driven workflows try to make agent output more predictable.
regions.whyItMatters: These tools let non-engineers build software and move the scarce skill from writing code to specifying what is wanted.
regions.openQuestion: Do prompt-built apps hold up in production, and do written specs actually make agent output more reliable?

landmarks.name: Lovable raises $400M at $13.3B
landmarks.summary: Series C co-led by Menlo Ventures and the EQT-managed Scaleup Europe Fund doubled the Swedish prompt-to-app builder's valuation from $6.6B in December 2025.

landmarks.name: Figma Make adoption lifts Figma results
landmarks.summary: Figma's Q4 2025 revenue rose 40% to $303.8M. Figma Make weekly users grew over 70% in the quarter, and over half of $100k+ customers used it weekly.

landmarks.name: GitHub Spec Kit released
landmarks.summary: GitHub open-sourced a toolkit that makes a written spec drive plans, task breakdowns and implementation by coding agents such as Copilot, Claude Code and Gemini CLI.

landmarks.name: AWS Kiro spec-driven IDE
landmarks.summary: Agentic IDE launched in preview around specs that turn a prompt into requirements, design and tasks before code, pitched as a step beyond vibe coding.

deepDives.title: Martin Fowler site: Understanding Spec-Driven Development
deepDives.why: Independent, sceptical comparison of Kiro, Spec Kit and Tessl by Birgitta Böckeler.

deepDives.title: GitHub Spec Kit
deepDives.why: The open toolkit for spec-driven development; read the method and try it.

deepDives.title: Kiro docs: Specs
deepDives.why: How a spec-first agentic IDE structures requirements, design and tasks.

deepDives.title: Design2Code: benchmarking front-end code generation
deepDives.why: Benchmark for how well multimodal models turn page designs into working code.

regions.name: Docs & codebase understanding
regions.summary: Tools auto-generate and refresh wikis, diagrams and Q&A for repositories, and serve docs and project context to agents via MCP. Accuracy still needs human checking.
regions.whyItMatters: Agents and new engineers are only as good as their understanding of the codebase, so context tooling shapes everything else.
regions.openQuestion: Can generated documentation stay accurate enough to trust without a human owner?

landmarks.name: Google Code Wiki preview
landmarks.summary: Gemini-powered wiki in public preview that regenerates docs for public repositories after each code change, with a chat agent grounded in the repo.

landmarks.name: Cognition DeepWiki
landmarks.summary: Free public version of Devin's wiki and search for any public GitHub repo, launched with over 50,000 repos indexed. An MCP server followed later in May 2025.

landmarks.name: Context7 MCP docs server launched
landmarks.summary: Upstash released an MCP server that feeds current, version-specific library documentation to coding agents, to counter answers based on outdated training data.

landmarks.name: AGENTS.md joins Agentic AI Foundation
landmarks.summary: OpenAI contributed the AGENTS.md format to the Linux Foundation's new Agentic AI Foundation, alongside Anthropic's MCP and Block's goose.

deepDives.title: AGENTS.md
deepDives.why: The shared format for giving agents project context; its site cites 60k+ projects.

deepDives.title: RepoAgent: repository-level code documentation generation
deepDives.why: Open framework and paper on generating and maintaining docs for a whole repository.

deepDives.title: The /llms.txt file
deepDives.why: Proposal for a standard file that points models at a site's key documentation.

deepDives.title: Context7
deepDives.why: See how up-to-date library docs are delivered to agents over MCP.

deepDives.title: SWE-bench Leaderboards
deepDives.why: The standard benchmark of real GitHub issues that coding agents are scored on.

deepDives.title: METR: We are Changing our Developer Productivity Experiment Design
deepDives.why: Careful account of why measuring AI speedup for developers is hard.

deepDives.title: The Pragmatic Engineer
deepDives.why: Widely read newsletter on how engineering teams actually use AI tools.

deepDives.title: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025: AI
deepDives.why: Large survey: 84% use or plan to use AI tools, yet more distrust than trust the output.

deepDives.title: Terminal-Bench
deepDives.why: Benchmark of realistic terminal tasks, widely quoted in coding model launches.
